title: Characterizations of a dominant morphism of integral algebraic spaces having transcendence degree zero

difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of five conditions for a dominant locally of finite type morphism of integral algebraic spaces — vanishing of the transcendence degree at the generic points, finiteness of the residue field extension, finiteness over suitable nonempty affine opens, quasi-finiteness at the generic point, and uniqueness of the point over the generic point of the target — and, when the morphism is separated or quasi-compact, also finiteness over some nonempty open of the target (statement lines 603-624). The proof (proof lines 626-664) reduces the first three conditions to the case of schemes through the schematic loci, compares transcendence degrees, uses specializations in the fibre for the uniqueness condition, and finishes with the dense open finiteness lemma. H2: a six-condition equivalence with four inputs, written out in full.
